title: PINN Failure-Mode Diagnostics
description: A challenge-oriented map connecting thirteen pathologies to symptoms, methodological responses, targeted improvements, and verification.
represents: The map starts with what fails and why, translates the failure into observable signatures, proposes targeted methodological responses, and states what should improve. It supports diagnostic reasoning from evidence rather than indiscriminate method substitution.
interpretation: A symptom can have several interacting causes, and a response may introduce new trade-offs. The map supports hypothesis generation, not automatic prescription. Every intervention must be checked with numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, and computational-cost criteria; if the evidence does not improve, re-diagnose the dominant failure mode.

categories.title: Inference / Reuse / Reliability
categories.summary: Supports inference, reuse, and trustworthy predictions

modes.title: Spectral bias / multiscale or high-frequency solution
modes.improvement: Better resolution of oscillatory and multiscale structures

evidence.rationale: The paper identifies eigenvector bias and shows Fourier features improving multi-scale PDE learning, directly supporting the spectral-bias diagnosis and response.
SAS-PINN uses SIREN high-frequency representation with adaptive collocation for stiff electromagnetic fields.
Locally adaptive activations with slope recovery provide an alternative basis and improve difficult PINN training.

modes.title: Discontinuities, shocks, or sharp fronts
symptoms: Large local error despite low global loss
modes.improvement: Improved admissibility and localized accuracy near discontinuities

evidence.rationale: wPINNs use a weak formulation to approximate entropy solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws, directly addressing shocks and discontinuities.
Conservative PINNs use subdomains and interface flux continuity for discontinuous conservation-law problems.

modes.title: Weak satisfaction of BCs / ICs / interfaces
modes.improvement: More reliable constraint satisfaction and physical consistency

evidence.rationale: The original neural trial-solution method embeds boundary conditions in the ansatz, directly supporting exact boundary fitting as a response.
The study directly evaluates exact Dirichlet enforcement in PINNs and VPINNs, supporting a hard-constraint response to persistent boundary error.
A hard-constraint PINN is constructed to satisfy governing conditions across multiple forward PDE cases.
Equality-constrained neural training supplies a constraint-based alternative to fixed penalty competition.

modes.title: Poor conservation (flux / mass / energy)
symptoms: Low pointwise error but large balance error
modes.improvement: Improved local and global physical fidelity through conservation

evidence.rationale: The conservative PINN formulation enforces local conservation and interface flux continuity, matching the diagnosed balance error and targeted response.

modes.title: High-order derivative cost or instability
modes.improvement: Reduced derivative order, memory, and runtime cost

evidence.rationale: High-order and high-dimensional automatic differentiation is identified as a memory and computation bottleneck and reduced through trace estimation.
Coupled automatic–numerical differentiation improves efficiency and robustness when conventional AD residuals are costly or sparse.

modes.title: Imbalanced multi-objective loss (gradient conflict)
symptoms: PDE loss decreases while BC / IC error remains high
modes.improvement: Better balance among objectives and improved trainability

evidence.rationale: The paper identifies competitive multi-term losses and automatically updates weights to restore balance.
Numerical stiffness is linked to unbalanced back-propagated gradients, with gradient-statistic annealing as the response.
Negative gradient interaction between PDE and boundary objectives is treated as a multi-objective conflict through dual-cone descent.

modes.title: Poor collocation / sampling coverage
symptoms: Low training loss but large unsampled error
modes.improvement: Better allocation of points and improved accuracy where needed

evidence.rationale: Residual-point placement is shown to control accuracy, and RAD/RAR-D dynamically move points toward under-resolved regions.
Loss-proportional importance sampling improves convergence by concentrating collocation effort where it is informative.
APINN uses a trainable gating network and shared subnetworks for soft domain and function decomposition.
XPINN provides spatial and temporal decomposition, local network specialization, interface coupling, and parallelization.
Distributed domain decomposition demonstrates strong scaling and reusable inference on domains much larger than the training domain.

modes.title: Long-time integration / temporal propagation
symptoms: Cannot learn the entire interval simultaneously
modes.improvement: Improved temporal stability and long-time prediction

evidence.rationale: Time-piecewise PINNs improve long-time-domain training by assigning independently adjustable subnetworks to temporal pieces.
XPINN explicitly supports time-domain decomposition and local temporal specialization.

modes.title: Optimization stagnation / ill-conditioning
modes.improvement: Better conditioning and faster, more stable convergence

evidence.rationale: The paper links differential operators to an ill-conditioned PINN loss landscape and compares first-order, hybrid, and second-order remedies.
Optimization-process analysis examines attainable accuracy and optimizer competitiveness rather than treating stagnation as an architecture-only issue.
Genetic initialization followed by L-BFGS supplies a staged response intended to improve stability and final accuracy.

modes.title: Sparse / noisy data, non-identifiable inverse problem
symptoms: Multiple parameter sets fit the data
Good state fit but wrong parameters

evidence.rationale: B-PINNs combine physical laws and scattered noisy measurements for forward and inverse inference while quantifying aleatoric uncertainty.
The method separates parametric and approximation uncertainty and uses uncertainty to guide new sensor placement.

modes.title: Repeated-query cost / retraining for new instances
symptoms: High cost per new parameter set

evidence.rationale: Physics-informed DeepONets learn a reusable solution operator and report rapid prediction across parametric PDE instances.
GPT-PINN reuses selected pretrained PINNs in a compact meta-network for parametric systems.
P2INNs avoid repetitive training by learning a latent representation across parameterized PDEs.
Separable PI-DeepONet reduces high-dimensional operator-learning cost while retaining comparable accuracy.
Bayesian PINNs compare posterior estimators and show that predictive fit alone does not establish reasonable uncertainty under noisy data.
Total-uncertainty PINNs quantify both parametric and approximation uncertainty for forward and inverse stochastic problems.
Physics-informed variational inference supplies a probabilistic latent representation for stochastic forward and inverse equations.

verification.title: Verify improvement
verification.instruction: Check the intervention with numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, and computational-cost criteria. If performance does not improve, re-diagnose the dominant failure mode and revisit the design choices.

evidence.rationale: The review supports evaluating physics-informed models through numerical, physical, robustness, uncertainty, and computational criteria rather than one loss value.
